title: tenet content file
description: One small named power the player buys with Codex (§4.2). The sum of the tenets you own is exactly what your Doctrine is allowed to say — which fields exist, how many rules each holds, which chips are legal, which modes and actions are offered. Nothing hands one over; you browse the list and spend.

name.description: Plain, not flavourful. This is a price tag on a shelf; the player has to know what they are buying without opening it.

desc.description: One sentence: what you can say afterwards that you could not say before.

section.description: Display grouping in the shop. Cosmetic; the sim knows nothing about it.

cost.description: Codex. A count of discoveries, not a farmable resource (§5) — so the whole list is deliberately unaffordable and what you buy is an argument about how you want to play.

requires.description: Prerequisites, not a price rise. A chip with nowhere to put it is not worth selling.

grants.description: Additive and order-independent — a union of sets and a sum of integers, so two players holding the same tenets hold the same capabilities whatever order they bought them in.

edit.description: Doctrine paths this opens for authoring. A path nothing grants does not appear in the panel at all.

slots.description: How many entries may sit at a path. Summed across every tenet that grants some.

forms.description: Expr forms legal in rules (§11.6). Structural forms — and, ≤, +, a number — are always free; the ones sold here are the forms that read a fact about the world.

modes.description: Targeting mode ids this makes selectable.

actions.description: Recruit actions this makes selectable — persuade, kill, decline.

groups.description: A whole form group at once, for a tenet that sells a way of saying things rather than a fact to say. Only `logic` and `compare` are free — arithmetic is bought, because thirteen maths chips in the dropdown of somebody who owns one tenet is the problem this design exists to fix.
